solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inadequate gear replaced after I object

indicators.note: things replaced are put back in a different arrangement, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: I as the object of a verb is me
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their replacement kit is not up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the rearranged gear behind ME, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre is a synonym describing an amount too small or poor to be sufficient.

clue.text: Girl catching the French disease

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a girl's name
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A young woman has contracted a French illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name is split after its first two letters to hold the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a mosquito-borne fever, an example of a disease.

clue.text: What students must pay for special treatment

blocks.note: first meaning: what you pay in class is heed to the teacher
second meaning: care or consideration lavished on someone

explanation.surface: It sounds as if students are charged a fee for extra favours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay' suggests money, but one pays heed, not cash, in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Students are told to pay attention, and attentions also means special care or courtesies shown to someone.

clue.text: Dismissal for not working after a sustained period

blocks.note: a run is an unbroken spell, like a run of luck
out means switched off or on strike

explanation.surface: Someone is sacked for being idle after a long stint in the job.
explanation.walkthrough: A run-out is a way a batsman is dismissed in cricket: the wicket is broken while he is short of his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run-out is one of the recognised ways a batsman can be given out, a kind of dismissal.

clue.text: Bishop worn out after argument with bully

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a row is a quarrel
beat means exhausted

explanation.surface: An exhausted bishop has a quarrel with a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' is a verb here, not a noun for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat is to intimidate with stern words, which is what a bully does; both work as verbs.

clue.text: Arsenal's second away defeat

indicators.note: the second means only the letter in position two of the word is kept

blocks.note: the second letter of the club's name
someone away is out

explanation.surface: A football report: Arsenal lose their second away match.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; here only its letter matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, overwhelming defeat, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Unrealistic of writer unknown to editor

blocks.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish writer
y is a mathematical unknown
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A fanciful book from an author the editor has never heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild-eyed schemes or dreamers are impractical and fanatical, so the word means unrealistic.

clue.text: One banished by king beheaded on French island

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A deposed king is sent to an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue sets the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished from their homeland.

clue.text: Centre of operations

blocks.note: surface reading: a headquarters from which a campaign or business is run
setter's reading: the place where surgeons operate, or the zone where armies fight

explanation.surface: It reads like a description of a command headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Both a hospital room for surgery and a military zone of fighting share this one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery happens in the operating theatre, and a war zone is called a theatre of operations.

clue.text: Not apparent in most recent books

blocks.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Something is not obvious in the newest publications.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent describes something present but hidden or dormant, not yet visible.

clue.text: Poins, drunk on it, coming round before the end of the game

indicators.note: turning round means the little word faces the other way

blocks.note: full is slang for tipsy
taken as written, to be turned round
Poins is the setter, who calls himself me

explanation.surface: The setter, the worse for drink, comes to just before the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's own name stands for ME. Pieces read FULL, the turned TI, then ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-time is the point in sport when the referee blows the final whistle and play stops.

clue.text: Closely examine letter's opening after lawyer indicateS something injurious to one's reputation

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: to scan is to scrutinise
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone reads a lawyer's letter closely and finds it defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The lawyer is an American District Attorney. The word 'indicateS' in the clue looks garbled in the source and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgraceful event or rumour that damages someone's good name.

clue.text: Trapped in city church, Ugandan extremists give up

indicators.note: extremes are the ends of a word, so the first and last letters are kept
something trapped is held inside the surrounding words

blocks.note: Reno, the city in Nevada
the outermost letters of the word
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Ugandan militants cornered in a cathedral city surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno is a city in Nevada; the church here is the Church of England, split around the captured letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to formally abandon a claim or belief, a synonym for give up.

clue.text: Overthrow annulment

blocks.note: first meaning: to beat or bring down
second meaning: the legal voiding of something, a dated sense

explanation.surface: A regime toppled and its laws cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeat is a verb for beating an opponent, and in law it once meant making a deed void.

clue.text: Betrayal of the Spanish left revealed after Suárez's inauguration

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so only the first letter counts

blocks.note: the first letter of the name
el is Spanish for the
L is the abbreviation for left
a secret revealed is out

explanation.surface: A Spanish leftist leader is exposed as a traitor at the start of Suárez's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the pieces behind the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sellout is an act of treachery, abandoning principles or allies for gain.

clue.text: A song about a song

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A song written about another song.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: Confirmed version of trainee vet

indicators.note: a new version is a different rendering, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An established form of the veterinary trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confirmed' as in a confirmed bachelor, set in their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Inveterate means long-established and unlikely to change, like a confirmed habit.

clue.text: Short piece in newspaper under "TV presenter becomes religious recluse"

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter is dropped
in a down clue, being under means sitting lower in the column, so the newspaper piece goes second

blocks.note: an anchor presents a news programme
an item is a short article

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline: a TV presenter gives it all up to become a hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' sets the shortened ITEM below ANCHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a person who withdraws from the world for prayer, a hermit.

clue.text: Funny bone by the sound of it

indicators.note: these words tell the solver to go by how something is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: the humerus is the upper arm bone

explanation.surface: It reads as a remark about the funny bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The funny bone is a nerve at the elbow near the humerus, which is the joke behind the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous is a direct synonym for amusing or comic.

clue.text: Brutus was reportedly clever about entering some time earlier

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: an hour is a length of time
on means concerning
able means capable

explanation.surface: A historian's remark that Brutus was said to be clever earlier in his career.
explanation.walkthrough: ON enters HOUR to make HONOUR, which comes earlier than ABLE. Mark Antony's speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar repeats that 'Brutus is an honourable man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony's funeral speech calls Brutus an honourable man again and again, ironically, so that is how he is reported.

clue.text: Article by Democrat after Bush failed to manage thriftily

indicators.note: something that failed has collapsed into a mess, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an is the indefinite article
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A political piece on a Democrat's budgeting after President Bush's failures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is the verb here, not the spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them sparingly and carefully, a verb sense distinct from spouse.

clue.text: A passage from Voltaire's Candide to glance over quickly

indicators.note: a passage taken from text is a run of consecutive letters lifted out of it

blocks.note: the letters run across the apostrophe and into the next word

explanation.surface: Someone skims an extract from Voltaire's satirical novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page can mean to skim it rapidly, the opposite of its other sense of close reading.

clue.text: Put at a loss when finally close to something positive

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
on can mean next to, as in a house on the river
a plus is an advantage

explanation.surface: Someone is stumped just when a good result was nearly in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to bewilder them so they don't know what to do.

clue.text: Lay out trendy underwear

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a vest in Britain is an undershirt

explanation.surface: Someone sets out fashionable underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay out' looks like arranging the clothes, but it means spending money.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is to spend it, and investing is putting money into something for a return.

clue.text: Jacob's son's son receiving money daughter left

indicators.note: left here means departed, so that letter goes away
receiving means taking in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a dime is a US ten-cent coin
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family-tree puzzle: a grandson gets some cash when a daughter departs.
explanation.walkthrough: The money is the American ten-cent coin, which loses its daughter abbreviation before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Simeon is the second of the twelve sons of Jacob.

clue.text: Author's explosive line retained

indicators.note: retained means kept within, so a piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a mine is an explosive device
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A writer's incendiary sentence survives the edit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' looks like an anagram signal for line, but it is the noun mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne is the English author who wrote Winnie-the-Pooh.

clue.text: Reject performer on the spot

blocks.note: a turn is a variety act or performer
money down is paid immediately

explanation.surface: A performer is refused at the audition, then and there.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a music-hall act; cash down is cash paid right away.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to refuse it, the same as rejecting it.

clue.text: Catch on at last after son takes Georgia back

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept
going back means the abbreviation is written in the other direction

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the last letter of the word
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A fish finally bites once a son takes Georgia home.
explanation.walkthrough: S, then N, then GA reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden problem or drawback, the kind of catch in a deal.

clue.text: Completely circular and having a great many uses

blocks.note: first meaning: round in every direction
second meaning: versatile

explanation.surface: Praise for a perfectly round, versatile gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-round player or tool is versatile, able to do many jobs well.

clue.text: Friendly spirit mostly seen near a lake

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a genie is a spirit of Arabian legend
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A kindly ghost is often spotted by a lakeside.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means warm and good-natured, a synonym for friendly.

clue.text: Doctor, say, grabbing animal from behind at European equestrian event

indicators.note: read from the back, the word runs in the opposite direction
grabbing means seizing and holding, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
e.g. means for example
an ass is a donkey
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A vet seizes a horse from the rear at a European show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for e.g., meaning for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the Olympic horse-riding discipline of precise, trained movements.

clue.text: Similar to accepting further capital

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: as means like
then means moreover, besides

explanation.surface: Like a city that welcomes more investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.
